subject: Bake-off criteria and benchmark request — Redwood vs vLLM/TGI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@datasynth.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Bake-off criteria and benchmark request — Redwood vs vLLM/TGI

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks again for your time earlier — good conversation. Below is a short recap from our discovery call and a proposal for the bake-off criteria so we can align expectations before we kick off testing.

Quick recap (pain points you shared)
- Inconsistent 95th percentile latency under production traffic; spikes during batch jobs and retries.
- High per-token cost from cloud-hosted endpoints at peak; experimenting with TGI on k8s but managing tail latency/ops is heavy.
- Need for predictable degradation and quick fallbacks when capacity is constrained.
- Auditability: retention of request/response logs and per-request metadata for compliance.

Current stack you described
- Production: TGI serving on in-house k8s cluster for 2x models (open-llama-30b variants).
- Experiments: vLLM on dedicated machines for lower latency tests.
- Cloud endpoints used for burst capacity (managed provider).

Primary success criteria for the bake-off (as discussed)
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for 512-token requests at target QPS (see throughput below).
- Throughput: sustain 200 concurrent QPS (512 token avg) with stable latency profile.
- Cost: total inference cost <= $X per 1M tokens (we'll refine target once you share current billing).
- Quality parity: model outputs must match your existing baseline for the provided eval prompt set (we'll use the sample prompts you promised).
- Operational: per-route observability (token-level cost, traces) and audit logs retained for 90 days.

Proposed benchmark matrix (what we'll run)
1) Baseline: your current TGI k8s setup (you run and share results or we run if you give access).
2) vLLM: open-vLLM configuration you're testing.
3) Redwood hosted/private footprints: running same model variants (quantized + FP16 where applicable) with three execution profiles (low-latency, balanced, cost-optimized).

Key metrics to collect (please confirm)
- P50/P95/P99 latency for 64/256/512/1024 token sequences.
- Tokens/sec and sustained QPS.
- Memory (max resident) and GPU VRAM usage.
- Cold-start latency for empty KV cache and warmed-cache latency.
- Cost per 1M tokens (based on actual resource usage).

Attachments: Benchmark_Spec_Datasynth.xlsx — contains the exact test harness, dataset specs, and acceptance criteria fields.

Timeline proposal
- You share a sample prompt set + 48 hours of production traces or a sanitized trace (or an AWS role) by Tue 2026-03-17.
- We provision test environments and run baseline + Redwood profiles within 7 business days of access.
- Initial benchmark report + executive one-pager delivered within 10 business days.

Questions for you
1) Can you confirm the target QPS we should use for the 512-token test? (200 is my placeholder assumption).
2) Will you provide a sanitized production trace or prefer to provide an AWS role for us to run tests against your staging cluster?
3) Any hard requirements on embeddings/reranking endpoints to include in the test?

If that looks right, I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet (attached) and our proposed NDA/procurement note so your procurement team can review pricing/terms in parallel.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@datasynth.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bake-off criteria and benchmark request — Redwood vs vLLM/TGI

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches my notes. A few clarifications so we can get you access quickly:

- QPS: 200 is fine for the 512-token test as a starting point. We also want a 50 QPS steady-state test to reflect low-latency lookup traffic.
- Dataset: I'll share a 1k-sample prompt set (sanitized) and a 48-hour trace from production (timestamps + token counts). Expect that by 2026-03-17 EOD.
- Environment: We prefer Redwood run tests in our AWS account (IAM role) so you exercise the exact network/storage profile. I'll coordinate with infra.
- Acceptance: If Redwood meets the P95 and cost targets for the balanced profile, we'll consider Redwood for a limited production pilot on Dedicated capacity (H1 plan).

I attached a small doc with our current monthly inference spend and model variants to help you size tests. Also: please include a cold-start scenario and a spike test (2x normal QPS for 5 minutes).

Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, Datasynth Inc.
sanjay@datasynth.io | +1 (617) 555-0934

--
Attachment: Datasynth_Current_Inference_Spend.pdf (1 page)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: (internal)
Date: 2026-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bake-off criteria and benchmark request — Redwood vs vLLM/TGI

Marissa, quick internal tech note for the proposed tests — copying what we'll need from Datasynth and what I'll run on the bench: 

- Test harness: use loadgen based on the attached spreadsheet (per-prompt timing + jitter). Recommend gpt-loadgen variant that supports KV cache warm/cold toggles.
- Model variants: open-llama-30b fp16 baseline, 30b int8 (q4_0 / q4_k_m), and one 13b low-cost variant for cost-optimized profile.
- Batching: measure 1/4/8/16 batch sizes; Redwood's continuous batching will be profiled and we should show the batching overhead vs raw vLLM.
- Cache scenarios: run both cold-start (empty cache) and warmed cache (simulate steady-state for 30 minutes). Include a TTL eviction test.
- Memory: record max GPU memory and host memory; also log KV-sizes and slot utilization.
- Latency percentiles: p50/p95/p99; also capture 95th tail with and without retries.
- Environment: if running in Datasynth AWS account, request an IAM role and a small test S3 bucket to push logs. If they don't want cross-account access, we can provide an encrypted AMI/instance to run the harness.

I'll prepare a short runbook and the command lines for the exact CLI steps (docker images, env vars, runner configs). Recommend we mark a target date once Sanjay shares the traces.

Rishi
Senior Applied Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@datasynth.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bake-off criteria and benchmark request — Redwood vs vLLM/TGI

Sanjay — perfect, thanks for the confirmations and the spend doc. Action items and timeline below so procurement/infra have clear asks: 

Action items
- Datasynth: share the sanitized 1k prompt set + production trace by 2026-03-17 EOD and open an IAM role with the two permissions in the benchmark spreadsheet (S3 write, CloudWatch read) or confirm you want us to run an AMI instead.
- Datasynth: confirm whether embeddings/reranking endpoints should be included (you indicated not required for the first pass — we'll exclude unless you confirm).
- Redwood: run baseline + three Redwood profiles (low-latency, balanced, cost-optimized) and return the initial benchmark report within 7 business days of access.
- Redwood deliverables: raw benchmark logs, a condensed executive one-pager, and recommended configuration (batching, quantization profile).

Acceptance criteria (we'll use this to judge results)
- P95 for 512 tokens <= 250ms in balanced profile.
- Sustained 200 QPS at equivalent P95 for the balanced profile.
- Cold-start P95 not exceeding 1.2x warmed P95 for the balanced profile.
- Per-1M token cost within 15% of the target number you provided in your spend doc.

Next meeting: let's reconvene after the initial bench report — propose Thu 2026-03-26 10:00 AM PT to review results and go over procurement steps. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Attaching: Redwood_Proposal_Datasynth.pdf (pricing + pilot terms).

If anything changes on your side, flag it here and I'll adjust the runbook with Rishi. Looking forward to this — excited to show what Redwood can do.

Best,

Marissa Cole
